name: Lasalimu
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Namun, realisasi vokal panjang pada bahasa Lasalimu bukan merupakan fonemis melainkan fonetis semata. Dalam berkomunikasi panjang pendeknya vokal yang diproduksi oleh penutur tidak menjadi hambatan dalam pemahaman satu sama lain. Tampaknya vokal panjang itu terjadi karena pengucapan logat setempat (kolektif idiolek) yang diakibatkan karena terdapat tekanan pada suku kata penultima yang cenderung pengucapan vokalnya agak dipertahankan temponya sehingga terkesan ada perpanjangan vokal tertentu.
new_statements.translation: However, the realization of long vowels in Lasalimu is not phonemic but purely phonetic. In communication, the length or shortness of the vowels speakers produce is no obstacle to mutual understanding. It appears that the long vowel arises from the local manner of pronunciation (collective idiolect), caused by the fact that there is stress on the penultimate syllable, whose vowel tends to be pronounced with its tempo somewhat sustained, so that there is an impression of lengthening of certain vowels.
new_statements.citation: Sanjoko, Yohanis. 2015 [online 2017]. Perbandingan karakteristik fonem bahasa Indonesia dengan bahasa Lasalimu. Kandai 11(1): 55-67. Kendari: Kantor Bahasa Sulawesi Tenggara.
new_statements.locator: p. 64 (PDF page 10 of 13), section 'Kontras Vokal dan Variannya', right column
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK. Opened (13 pp., text layer; Kandai 11(1), Mei 2015, pp. 55-67, header on p. 1). extracted text of PDF page 10 (printed p. 64) contains the quoted passage word for word: "Namun, realisasi vokal panjang pada bahasa Lasalimu bukan merupakan fonemis melainkan fonetis semata. Dalam berkomunikasi panjang pendeknya vokal yang diproduksi oleh penutur tidak menjadi hambatan dalam pemahaman satu sama lain. Tampaknya vokal panjang itu terjadi karena pengucapan logat setempat (kolektif idiolek) yang diakibatkan karena terdapat tekanan pada suku kata penultima yang cenderung pengucapan vokalnya agak dipertahankan temponya sehingga terkesan ada perpanjangan vokal tertentu." Only locator nuan…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; the stressed penultimate vowel is often held longer, which the author treats as phonetic (non-phonemic) vowel lengthening.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. The same passage also lists phonetic long vowels in word-final position ([rampu:] 'bakar', [mobu:] 'berat', [ina:] 'ibu') and in the monosyllable [i:] 'di', which the penultimate-stress explanation does not cover; the author does not comment on this.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, in elicited citation forms from a wordlist-based phoneme study (Kecamatan Lasalimu, Kabupaten Buton). The stress remark is made in passing to explain vowel length; the article has no dedicated suprasegmental/stress section and gives no stress-marked examples.
new_statements.identity_note: Sanjoko 2015 describes 'bahasa Lasalimu' as spoken in Kecamatan Lasalimu, Kabupaten Buton, Sulawesi Tenggara = Lasalimu [llm] lasa1237 (Nusi 2012 places the Lasalimu villages in Kecamatan Lasalimu Selatan and Kamaru in Kecamatan Lasalimu). Firman A.D. 2017 treats Lasalimu and Kamaru (Kamaru [kgx] kama1364) as dialects of a single 'Lasalimu-Kamaru' language, as Pusat Bahasa 2008 does, whereas SIL 2006 and Glottolog keep them as two languages; the stress remark quoted is for the Lasalimu variety proper.

sources.note: Phoneme inventory and distribution of Lasalimu (20 consonants, 5 vowels); no dedicated suprasegmental section, but p. 64 attributes phonetic vowel lengthening to 'tekanan pada suku kata penultima' (stress on the penultimate syllable); vowel length is stated to be phonetic, not phonemic.
